description: Make the demo turn-key and presentation-ready for FREE: document the single command(s) to run the full populated+logged-in-capable stack, the demo login credentials, what is synthetic vs. real (the scraping honesty note), and FREE non-provisioning deployment options (local / GitHub Codespaces, and optionally a Dockerfile/docker-compose) WITHOUT provisioning any paid AWS/cloud resources. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003 being complete so the documented commands and credentials are accurate.
steps: Confirm `make demo` (scripts/demo.sh) still works as the single command: it seeds (`python -m app.seed`, now also creating the demo user) then launches both servers. The sandbox dev-server guard blocks launching live servers here, so verify the SEED step and the import/build paths, not a live listener: run `cd backend && uv run python -m app.seed` and confirm it is idempotent and creates the resort data + demo user; confirm scripts/demo.sh wiring (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, CORS, ports) is correct by reading it. Note in findings that live-server verification was done in-process via TestClient per the environment constraint.

Update README.md: (a) describe The Forest Season Resort as the demo's home property and the end-to-end story; (b) document the exact single command(s) to run the full stack for the presentation (make setup once, then make demo) and the dashboard URL; (c) document the DEMO LOGIN CREDENTIALS prominently (the owner/manager username + password seeded in FEAT-002) so the presenter can log in; (d) add/expand an HONESTY note: the review dataset is synthetic/representative, generated and run through the REAL ingestion/collection pipeline (Review_Collector -> parse -> language/sentiment/aspect -> normaliser -> market model -> changepoints), and genuine live scraping of Google/MakeMyTrip/Booking.com/TripAdvisor/Agoda is NOT performed because it requires each platform's official API/permission and must respect robots.txt + terms (responsible.py is the scrape-mode mechanism, kept for authenticity); (e) clearly state everything runs FREE with no third-party credentials.

Add a FREE LIVE-URL + deployment section to README.md (the user explicitly asked for a live URL to the site). Provide concrete, zero-cost ways to get a public URL WITHOUT provisioning paid AWS/cloud: (a) GitHub Codespaces forwarded port set to Public visibility -> gives an instant free https URL for the running Next.js app during the demo; (b) frontend on Vercel free tier + backend on a free tier (e.g. Render/Railway/Fly free) with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL pointed at the deployed API and CORS/FRONTEND_ORIGIN set accordingly - document the exact env vars to set; (c) a quick-share tunnel (e.g. `cloudflared tunnel` / ngrok free) over the local `make demo` for a temporary live URL. For each option give the exact steps and note it is FREE. Explicitly state NO paid AWS/cloud resources are provisioned by this project and that a real managed cloud deployment is a separate, explicitly-confirmed step. Do NOT add infra-as-code that spins up paid services. Make clear that this sandbox cannot itself open a public listener (dev-server guard), so the presenter runs one of these free options from their own machine/Codespace, or the orchestrator publishes.

To make the free live-URL options actually work, ensure the app is deploy-ready: confirm NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is read for the API base (it is, in lib/api.ts) and FRONTEND_ORIGIN/CORS is configurable (it is, in config.py). Add a frontend .env.example or document the single env var the presenter sets so the deployed frontend talks to the deployed backend. If a Vercel/Codespaces config file adds value and is free + non-provisioning (e.g. a vercel.json or a .devcontainer/devcontainer.json that runs make setup && make demo and forwards ports), add it; otherwise document the manual steps.

OPTIONAL (free, non-provisioning) containerization: if it adds demo value, add a Dockerfile (and/or docker-compose.yml) that builds the backend + frontend images for local/Codespaces use only, with a note that it provisions nothing in the cloud. Only do this if it can be kept green and does not complicate `make demo`; otherwise skip and say so in findings. If added, verify `docker build` works (OPEN_INTERNET allows image pulls) OR, if the sandbox cannot run docker, note that and validate the Dockerfile syntactically.
Update .env.example only if FEAT-002 introduced new auth/session config that a deployer must know about (e.g. document SESSION_SECRET usage for login); keep all defaults local/credential-free.

FINAL full verification pass: `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest` (all pass) and `cd frontend && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build` (all pass, final route count). Re-run `cd backend && uv run python -m app.seed` and a TestClient(app) smoke heredoc covering /health, /auth/login (demo creds -> token), /auth/me, /market-radar/review-counts (resort), /sentinel/board, /destination/heatmap, /concierge/facts to confirm the documented flow actually works. Record exact commands + credentials in findings for the orchestrator to relay.
acceptance_criteria: README documents the exact single command(s) to run the full stack (make setup; make demo), the dashboard URL, and the demo login credentials for The Forest Season Resort.

README has a clear honesty note: dataset is synthetic/representative run through the REAL ingestion pipeline; live platform scraping is not performed and requires official APIs/permission + robots.txt/terms compliance (responsible.py mechanism noted); everything runs FREE with no third-party credentials.

README has a FREE live-URL + deployment section giving concrete zero-cost ways to get a public URL (Codespaces public forwarded port, Vercel+free-tier backend with documented env vars, or a free tunnel over make demo) and explicitly states no paid AWS/cloud resources are provisioned by this project; the app is deploy-ready (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL + FRONTEND_ORIGIN/CORS documented).
If a Dockerfile/compose is added, it is for local/Codespaces only, provisions nothing in the cloud, and either builds cleanly or is noted as syntactically validated; make demo still works.
All quality gates green (backend ruff + pytest; frontend lint + vitest + build) and the final in-process smoke covering login + resort data passes.
verification: cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest
cd frontend && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build
cd backend && uv run python -m app.seed

cd backend && uv run python - <<'PY'
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
c=TestClient(app)
r=c.post('/auth/login', json={'username':'owner@forestseason.demo','password':'ForestSeason@2024'})
print('login', r.status_code)
tok=r.json().get('token') if r.status_code==200 else None
for p in ['/health','/market-radar/review-counts','/sentinel/board','/destination/heatmap','/concierge/facts']:
    print(p, c.get(p).status_code)
if tok: print('me', c.get('/auth/me', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {tok}'}).status_code)
PY
